meta.policy: Nothing in this file is used in any computed projection. It exists so the decision maker knows what could change the answer, and how.
meta.verification_standard: Each item is either (a) enacted and therefore in laws.json and in the model, or (b) merely proposed/announced and therefore here, excluded from the model, and labelled.

items.name: San Francisco Board of Supervisors File No. 261020 — temporary cap on banked and capital-improvement rent increases
items.jurisdiction: City and County of San Francisco
items.summary: Would temporarily limit the combined amount of banked rent increases and capital-improvement passthroughs on rent-controlled units to 10% per year.
items.effect_if_enacted: Caps upside on Property B's two rented units. Reduces the rent-growth assumption used for Property B, which lowers every scenario's terminal value roughly equally because Property B is held in all three — so it does not by itself change which scenario wins.
items.source_quote: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors is considering legislation (File No. 261020) that would temporarily limit the combined amount of banked rent increases and capital improvement rent increases that may be imposed on rent-controlled units to 10% per year. ... This legislation has not been enacted and is subject to change.

items.name: AB 1482 statewide rent cap sunset on January 1, 2030
items.status: enacted with a sunset — future extension unknown
items.summary: Civil Code §1947.12 states the section remains in effect only until January 1, 2030 and is repealed as of that date.
items.effect_if_enacted: If the Legislature does not extend it, statewide rent caps on Property A (if rented out) disappear after 2029, which is upside to the rent-out scenario and neutral to the others. If it is extended or expanded, the rent-out case weakens. Modelled at a flat 2%/yr rent growth across the whole horizon precisely because this is unresolved.
items.source_quote: (o) This section shall remain in effect until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.

items.name: Biennial re-indexation of the Prop 19 $1M amount
items.status: enacted mechanism — next adjustment February 2027, amount not yet published
items.summary: The $1,000,000 figure is adjusted every other February 16 to the FHFA California House Price Index. Current published value is $1,044,586 for transfers 2/16/2025–2/15/2027.
items.effect_if_enacted: If California house prices rise, the excluded amount rises and the heir keeps more of the parent's low base. Modelled by holding the 2026-published cap flat, so the model is conservative against the heir on this one point.
items.source_quote: The next adjustment of the $1 million amount will occur in February 2027.

items.name: Federal estate-tax exclusion indexation after 2026
items.status: enacted mechanism — forward amounts not yet published
items.summary: The basic exclusion is $15,000,000 for 2026 and is indexed for inflation from 2027. The IRS has not published 2027+ figures.
items.effect_if_enacted: Every future-year exclusion will be higher than $15,000,000, so the estate-tax exposure modelled here is an upper bound (a floor on the exclusion is a ceiling on the tax).

items.name: California wealth-tax proposals
items.summary: Recurring proposals to tax extremely large holdings annually. None is enacted law as of the research date.
items.effect_if_enacted: Would only bite at holdings far above the figures in this plan. Not modelled. Listed so the decision maker knows it is on the radar, NOT as a projection input.
items.flag: No primary source confirmed an enacted or pending bill text in this research pass. Deliberately left unsourced and excluded. Treat as unverified.

items.name: California estate tax reintroduction proposals
items.summary: Periodic legislative proposals to create a California estate tax. California currently has none (State Controller's Office confirms no California estate tax return is required for deaths on or after 1/1/2005).
items.effect_if_enacted: Would add a state-level tax on the estate itself, on top of the federal tax. Not modelled because nothing is enacted.
items.source_quote: For decedents that die on or after January 1, 2005, there is no longer a requirement to file a California Estate Tax Return.

items.name: Net Energy Metering grandfathering for existing solar
items.status: enacted — the applicable tariff depends on a date not supplied
items.summary: NEM tariffs are closed to new enrollments; interconnections applied for on or after 4/15/2023 take the Net Billing Tariff at avoided-cost export values. Existing systems keep the tariff in force when they interconnected.
items.effect_if_enacted: Determines whether Property A's solar continues to generate a retail-rate credit or drops to a much smaller export credit. Modelled as a −$15/month credit with a $0 floor sensitivity because the interconnection date is unknown.
items.source_quote: These tariffs are closed to new enrollments. ... Since April 15, 2023, customers applying for interconnection have taken service on the new net billing tariff (NBT)
